title: Pennsylvania State Government Websites: ADA Title II PDF Accessibility | SignalFeed.dev
description: How Pennsylvania state-government websites stand on PDF accessibility before the April 26, 2027 ADA Title II date: 36% of 336 sampled PDFs untagged, 6% scanned. Aggregate, automated signals.
h1: Pennsylvania: Title II PDF backlog on state government websites
body:
We found 11 working state-government websites on .gov domains registered to Pennsylvania in CISA's public .gov registry. State governments are Title II public entities, and all of them reach the ADA Title II web rule's compliance date on April 26, 2027 (28 CFR part 35, subpart H): web content, PDFs included, must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to the rule's exceptions.

Does ADA Title II apply to Pennsylvania?

Yes. Title II is federal law and covers Pennsylvania's state agencies and public universities, counties, cities, towns, school districts and special districts; the PDF guide covers the rule's exceptions. This is general information, not legal advice.

We measured the PDFs these sites link from their pages. This page summarizes Pennsylvania's state-government sites as a whole. It does not name or rank individual agencies. Agencies on non-.gov addresses are not included. For cities and counties, see the city and county editions.

Pennsylvania at a glance

  • 6 of 11 state-government sites measured with a usable sample (20 or more PDFs). Of the rest, 0 blocked our crawler and 5 could not be sampled: too few PDFs on the main site (some host documents on other systems) or a crawl that only partly finished. That is not a clean result.
  • 336 PDFs analyzed. 35.7% had no accessibility tags, close to the national figure of 37.7%. 5.7% were scanned images with no usable text, 39.9% did not declare a document language, and 53% had no document title.
  • Spread: on 2 of the 6 measured sites more than half the sampled PDFs were untagged; on 2, fewer than 1 in 10 were. No single main issue dominated: no document title and missing accessibility tags led on 2 sites each.
  • 0 of 18 sampled PDFs passed the veraPDF PDF/UA-1 checks.
  • The median measured site has roughly 1,500 pages of PDFs failing at least one basic check; across the measured sites that is on the order of 25,000 pages.
  • 66% of the sampled PDFs were modified in 2024 or later. Recent documents are more likely to still be in active use, and documents used to apply for, access or participate in a service are not covered by the rule's exception for preexisting documents.

What this means for Pennsylvania agencies

An untagged PDF gives a screen reader no headings, reading order or table structure, and a scanned one gives it nothing; both typically fail WCAG 2.1 AA and are common in reports, rules, forms and notices. Archived content and preexisting documents are exempt unless people use them to get a service, so the usual order is: fix export settings, remediate forms and service documents, then move true archives to a marked archive section.

For agendas, minutes and notices, our accessible meeting templates for small public bodies ($24, Word + PDF/UA) export tagged PDFs from Word, so new documents start out accessible.

What this is, and what it isn't

These are automated signals scaled from samples, not a conformance evaluation: a check can show a PDF fails, not that it conforms. Method: national Backlog Index page.
